column1: # Names and modules that are NOT part of the Win32-common surface, although a
# name match says otherwise.  Read by tools/ce_api_names.py (see its docstring)
# and consumed by tools/fetch-upstream.py, tools/build-win32-map.py and
# tools/check-policy.py, so the whole repository agrees on one surface.
#   name    an API name that must not be matched: Windows CE documents a
#           different thing with that name, so the Win32 page is not CE material
#   module  an sdk-api module whose APIs Windows CE never had at all
# Keep this short and reviewed: every line is a documented exception, not a
# place to hide pages that simply look odd.  The evidence for everything else is

column3: CE's "Address" (Windows CE 3.0 Device Driver Development) is the display driver's entry point, not the dbghelp ADDRESS structure
CE's "Run (Windows Media Player)" is not the winddi.h RUN structure (Windows CE has no printer-driver RUN)
Windows Runtime (RoInitialize, RoGetActivationFactory, ...) - never on Windows CE
Core Audio device topology (Windows Vista and later)
Windows Contacts (contacts.h); the CE IContact of the same name is the Pocket Outlook Object Model contact object
Desktop Task Scheduler (mstask.h); the CE ITask of the same name is the Pocket Outlook Object Model task object
The upstream "tag" helper of that module is unrelated to the Mobile Channels TAG name CE documents
